title: CatESO: Differentiable Enzyme Sequence Optimization Guided by Substrate-Aware Kcat Prediction.
authors: Gan, Zhenjia; Xu, Yuzhi; Xu, Junde; Wu, Zhihao; Huang, Juping; Yin, Jiabin; Chen, Guangyong; Zhang, John Z H
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
one_liner_zh: 该文提出CatESO，一种通过可微序列优化直接以底物感知的Kcat预测为引导的酶序列设计方法，将动力学目标与序列生成端到端结合，属于蛋白质序列设计并兼顾结构完整性，与课题高度相关。
abstract: Enzymes drive biological chemistry and offer greener routes to chemicals, materials, and medicines, yet their broader use as biocatalysts is often limited by insufficient catalytic turnover. Improving turnover is hard: measured rate constants are scarce and protein sequence space is vast. Deep learning models now predict the turnover number, Kcat, with growing accuracy, but they are typically applied after sequence generation to score or filter candidates, which separates the kinetic objective from the design itself. To bridge the gap between sequence generation and kinetic evaluation, we introduce CatESO, a differentiable sequence optimizer that enables direct, gradient-guided design of substrate-specific catalytic turnover. By backpropagating through a cross-modal Kcat predictor under continuous sequence relaxation, CatESO co-optimizes predicted catalytic activity, evolutionary plausibility, and structural integrity in one end-to-end framework, using ESM-2 and ESMFold to keep designs evolutionarily plausible and foldable. Across seven stringent, out-of-distribution enzymes spanning EC classes 1-7, CatESO raised model-predicted Kcat for many designs, with a median predicted fold change of 1.52, while every variant retained a pLDDT above 70. Against the RFdiffusion3-LigandMPNN pipeline and ZymCtrl, CatESO struck a better balance between predicted activity and structural confidence. By making substrate-conditioned kinetic objectives differentiable, CatESO carries differentiable protein design beyond structure- and binding-centered goals to enzyme catalytic function, giving a general route to function-oriented enzyme engineering.
abstract_zh: 酶驱动生物化学反应，并为化学品、材料及药物提供更绿色的合成途径，然而其作为生物催化剂的更广泛应用常受限于催化周转不足。提升周转率颇具挑战：实测速率常数稀缺，且蛋白质序列空间庞大。深度学习模型现能以日益增长的准确性预测周转数Kcat，但它们通常在序列生成后用于评分或筛选候选，这使动力学目标与设计本身相分离。为弥合序列生成与动力学评估之间的鸿沟，我们引入CatESO，一种可微分的序列优化器，能够实现底物特异性催化周转的直接、梯度引导设计。通过在连续序列松弛下对跨模态Kcat预测器进行反向传播，CatESO在一个端到端框架中协同优化预测催化活性、进化合理性和结构完整性，利用ESM-2和ESMFold确保设计在进化上合理且可折叠。在涵盖EC类别1-7的七个严格、分布外酶中，CatESO提升了许多设计的模型预测Kcat，中位预测倍数变化为1.52，同时每个变体的pLDDT均保持在70以上。与RFdiffusion3-LigandMPNN流程及ZymCtrl相比，CatESO在预测活性与结构置信度之间取得了更佳平衡。通过使底物条件化的动力学目标可微分，CatESO将可微分蛋白质设计从结构和结合中心目标拓展至酶催化功能，为面向功能的酶工程提供了一条通用途径。
